notes: 1912 four-storey flats, greige horizontal wood siding with cream trim over a buff glazed-brick street storey with a recessed entry left of centre. One cant bay on the left half from storey 2 to the roof, flat paired windows under it on storey 1, a single window column on the right. The right half is inferred. The tinted brick kit rendered terracotta; the street storey is now a buff painted band so it reads as the cream glazed brick base. Khaki olive-grey lap siding, dark brown sash frames inside cream surrounds, windows in pairs on both halves, a shallow bay on the real left (the still is mirrored by the world east-west mirror), buff brick street storey with a recessed dark wood entry and a sidelight. Darker warm mauve-taupe lap siding; two stacked cant bays from storey 1 to the roof (8 units over 4 storeys means two flats a floor, matching the neighbours' paired bay stacks) instead of one bay over a flat half; the pale full-height plinth is gone: a shorter street storey (floorsM) in darkened buff brick with a dark recessed entry porch zone around the stair door and sidelight. Only colours from the blur applied: ground band greyish olive, cornice/trim dark brown (no bright white band visible). No geometry change. Base recoloured beige-grey b3ab9a so it is not the sage/olive neighbour. Clapboard fix (2026-10-02): painted siding moved from the stained-timber wood-siding base to painted-clapboard so the tint renders as paint, not olive. Tint lift (2026-10-02): wall tints lifted toward the sunlit paint (t' = 1-(1-t)k).
